findings.what: chatsToPostStoriesWithCompletion: resolves the title of every chat id with -nameForUserId:, which is only a lookup in usersById: `NSString *title = [weakSelf nameForUserId:chatId.longLongValue] ?: @"";`
findings.failure: getChatsToPostStories returns the user's own chat id plus the ids of channels the user administers. Channel ids are negative (-100...) and are never keys in usersById, so their title comes back as @"". The story composer's chat picker in src/TGStoriesViewController.m:2041-2043 does `NSString *title = TGStoryString(chat, @"title"); if (title.length == 0) continue;` — every channel row is silently dropped, so the user can never post a story as a channel, and if the own user record is not yet cached the action sheet appears with zero options. The same wrong helper is used at TGClient+Stories.m:441 (story viewer names: channel reposters show blank), :801 (hiddenStoryPosters) and :1183 (storyNotificationExceptions, which are chat ids).
findings.fix: Add one shared name-for-message-sender helper and use it at all four sites: for id > 0 use -nameForUserId:, for id < 0 look the id up in self.chatsById[@(id)][@"title"] (TGClient+Private.h:25) and fall back to scanning client.chats/archivedChats — TGClient+Reactions.m:101 TGReactionSenderName() already implements exactly this and is the correct version.

findings.what: streamFile:offset:count:completion: treats the file's `prefixSize` as bytes available at the requested offset: `long long available = [file[@"prefixSize"] longLongValue]; long long wanted = available < count ? available : count;`
findings.failure: `prefixSize` is TDLib's local.downloaded_prefix_size, which is counted from local.download_offset, not from the caller's `offset`. When the file already has bytes from a previous range (download_offset = 0) and the player asks for offset = 2_000_000, prefixSize can be larger than what actually exists at that offset, so -readFile:offset:count: is issued with a count that runs past the downloaded region; readFilePart returns an error, the completion gets nil, and the AVAssetResourceLoader range fails — video playback stalls with no retry.
findings.fix: Compute the availability relative to the request: `long long base = [file[@"downloadOffset"] longLongValue]; long long end = base + [file[@"prefixSize"] longLongValue]; long long available = end - offset;` (clamp to 0), or simply re-call -downloadedPrefixSizeForFile:offset: after the download completes and use that value as `wanted`.

findings.what: TGFileOfMessageContent reads a photo size without a type guard: `file = TGFilesDict([sizes lastObject][@"photo"]);` — every other branch in this function wraps its lookups in TGFilesDict(), this one subscripts the raw last element.
findings.failure: If TDLib's `photo.sizes` vector ever contains anything other than a dictionary (malformed/unexpected reply, or a future schema where sizes carries plain values), `-objectForKeyedSubscript:` is sent to e.g. an NSString or NSNumber and the app dies with 'unrecognized selector sent to instance' while building the downloads list in searchDownloadsWithQuery:.
findings.fix: Change to `file = TGFilesDict(TGFilesDict([sizes lastObject])[@"photo"]);`, matching the guarded style used in the messageDocument/messageVideo branches above it and in TGClient+Stories.m:79.

findings.what: The reaction watch timer polls one full getMessage per watched message every tick: inside -tgReactionWatchTick: `for (NSString *key in [TGReactionWatches allKeys]) { ... [self reactionChipsForMessage:messageId inChat:chatId completion:...] }` with TGReactionWatchInterval = 5.0.
findings.failure: TGChatViewController creates a TGReactionChipsView per reacted bubble (src/TGChatViewController.m:5183-5192) and each one registers a watch (src/TGReactionPickerView.m:1870). A chat screen with 10 reacted messages visible issues 10 getMessage round trips every 5 seconds, forever, on a single-core A5 — each reply is a full message JSON parsed on the main queue. Scrolling a busy group chat becomes visibly janky and the radio never idles, draining the battery.
findings.fix: Replace the poll with the TDLib push: handle `updateMessageInteractionInfo` in TGClient -handleUpdate: (it is currently not handled anywhere — `grep updateMessageInteractionInfo src` returns nothing), look the (chat_id, message_id) up in TGReactionWatches and fire the block from the update. Keep the timer only as a fallback with a much longer interval.

findings.what: -setReactionWatchInterval: only writes the static `TGReactionWatchInterval = seconds < 2.0 ? 2.0 : seconds;`, but -tgStartReactionWatchTimer (line 539-547) reads that value once when it creates the NSTimer and returns early ever after (`if (TGReactionWatchTimer) return;`).
findings.failure: Calling setReactionWatchInterval: after any chip view has started watching has no effect at all — the poll keeps running at whatever interval was in force when the first watch was registered. The method has no callers today, so it is both dead and broken; the first caller will silently get nothing.
findings.fix: Either delete the method and its header declaration, or make it invalidate and rebuild the timer: `[TGReactionWatchTimer invalidate]; TGReactionWatchTimer = nil; if (TGReactionWatches.count) [self tgStartReactionWatchTimer];`.

findings.what: -setStoryPreloading:onNetwork: builds the new settings from a preset instead of the current ones: `NSDictionary *base = TGStoryDict(presets[@"low"]); ... settings[@"preload_stories"] = @(preload); ... setAutoDownloadSettings`.
findings.failure: Toggling story preloading overwrites the user's whole auto-download configuration for that network with the 'low' preset — max photo/video/other file sizes, video_upload_bitrate and use_less_data_for_calls all silently reset. Additionally TGStoryNetworkType() (line 253) maps everything that is not @"wifi" to networkTypeMobile, so the roaming and 'other' network types can never be addressed.
findings.fix: Read the current settings first (getAutoDownloadSettings / the values TGClient+Network already exposes), mutate only preload_stories, and extend TGStoryNetworkType to map @"roaming" -> networkTypeMobileRoaming and @"other" -> networkTypeOther. Or delete the method — it currently has no callers.

findings.what: The same four-helper quartet is written independently in each file of this area: TGStoryIsError/TGStoryArray/TGStoryDict/TGStoryString (Stories.m:4-19), TGIsError/TGArray/TGDict/TGString (Stickers.m:4-19), TGFilesIsError/TGFilesArray/TGFilesDict/TGFilesString (Files.m:19-34), plus hand-rolled variants inline in Reactions.m (lines 262-263, 282-283, 334-335, 372-373, 641-642 all re-inline `![result isKindOfClass:NSDictionary.class] || [result[@"@type"] isEqualToString:@"error"]`).
findings.failure: The copies already disagree: TGStoryArray returns @[] on a non-array while TGArray/TGFilesArray return nil, and TGString returns nil where TGStoryString/TGFilesString return @"" — so identical-looking code in two files behaves differently on the same malformed reply. All three isError variants also send -isEqualToString: to an unchecked `result[@"@type"]`, which crashes if TDLib ever returns a non-string there.
findings.fix: Promote one set into TGClient+Private.h (e.g. TGIsError/TGArray/TGDict/TGString with documented nil-vs-empty behaviour, and `NSString *t = result[@"@type"]; return ![t isKindOfClass:NSString.class] ? YES : [t isEqualToString:@"error"];`), delete the per-file copies, and replace the five inline error checks in Reactions.m with it.

findings.what: A large slice of this area's public API has no caller anywhere outside the category itself. Verified with grep over src/*.m excluding TGClient+*: -streamFile:offset:count:completion:, -readFile:offset:count:completion:, -downloadFile:offset:limit:completion:, -minithumbnailData:, -storageStatisticsWithChatLimit:, -fileExtensionForMimeType:, -resolveRemoteFileId:type:completion:, -addFileToDownloads:inChat:messageId:priority:completion: (Files); -stickerOutlineForFileId:completion:, -installedStickersMatching:limit:completion:, -premiumStickersWithLimit:completion:, -greetingStickersWithCompletion:, and the completion-less -reorderInstalledStickerSets: (line 273) which is fully superseded by -reorderInstalledStickerSets:completion: (line 773, the one TGStickersViewController.m:1221 actually calls) (Stickers); -setStoryPreloading:onNetwork:, -resolveStoryLink:completion:, -searchStoriesWithTag:..., -publicForwardsOfStory:..., -setCloseFriends:, -closeFriendsWithCompletion:, -hiddenStoryPostersWithCompletion: (Stories); -setReactionWatchInterval: (Reactions).
findings.failure: No runtime failure, but roughly 500 lines of untested code and the base64 decoder that only -readFile:/-minithumbnailData: use are compiled into a binary running on a 512MB device, and the streaming trio carries the offset bug reported above without anything exercising it.
findings.fix: Delete the unreferenced methods and their header declarations, or, for the ones that are deliberate future API (the streaming trio for the video player), mark them in the header as unused and fix the streamFile offset bug before the first caller lands.

findings.what: TGFlattenSticker decides animation by negation: `@"isAnimated" : @(![format isEqualToString:@"stickerFormatWebp"])` where `format` defaults to @"" when the sticker object has no `format` member (line 47).
findings.failure: Any sticker whose `format` field is missing or arrives under an unexpected type is reported as isAnimated = YES. Callers treat animated stickers as undecodable on this device, so a perfectly ordinary static WebP sticker is rendered as a blank/placeholder cell instead of the image.
findings.fix: Invert the test to a positive one: `BOOL animated = [format isEqualToString:@"stickerFormatTgs"] || [format isEqualToString:@"stickerFormatWebm"];` so an unknown or missing format degrades to the static path.
